title: Settings Hub hardening: per-plugin capability, real integration tests, CI and docs realignment
description: Execution state for issue #48. Read this file at the start of every session and continue from the first work item that is not completed. After every finished task or commit: flip its status, append a dated log entry to the work item, add a changelog entry when the note is cross-cutting, and bump lastUpdated. Narrative and design live in docs/settings-hub-hardening-plan.md and are not rewritten to record progress.

taskTemplate.note: Every phase runs this lifecycle around its phase-specific tasks. One phase is one branch and one PR referencing #48. Phase 1 uses the issue branch 48-settings-hub-hardening; later phases use 48-phase-<n>-<slug> created from up-to-date main with `gh issue develop 48 --base main --name <branch>`.

steps.description: Create or check out the phase branch from up-to-date main and confirm the previous phase is merged.
Complete the phase-specific tasks listed in the work item.

Run composer phpcs, composer phpstan and the unit and integration suites against a real WordPress test install (WP_TESTS_DIR set, DB wp_settings_hub_test, root with an empty password on 127.0.0.1 locally).
Run core-review --budget medium (thorough for Phase 5), apply every critical and warning finding, and re-run until nothing new is reported.
Push, open the PR referencing #48 with this JSON updated in the same PR, and get CI green.

workItems.title: Phase 1: CI and tooling
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-settings-hub-hardening (already created and linked to #48; carries this plan). Make CI fail on what it claims to check, test the supported WordPress range, and block releases with a stale PACKAGE_VERSION. Known limitation: on a manual release dispatch the reusable quality-checks job still checks out the dispatching ref, not the tag; only validate and build use the tag.
findings: quality-checks.yml runs `composer phpcbf || true` before `composer phpcs`, so fixable style violations never fail CI.

integration-guide.php fails `php -l` (unexpected token "public" on line 475): a nested docblock at :456-474 closes the outer /* */ opened at :387. It is excluded from PHPCS and PHPStan, so nothing catches it.

actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 is commented `# v5.2.2` in ci.yml, quality-checks.yml and release.yml; that SHA is tag v7.0.1 and v5.2.2 does not exist. actions/github-script@v9 in auto-merge-dependabot.yml is a floating tag (v9 = 3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3). setup-php 2.40.0, cache v6.1.0, codecov v7.1.1 and action-gh-release v3.0.3 pins are correct.
CI installs WordPress 'latest' only and starts MySQL via apt/systemctl; the reference repo silver-assist-security uses a mysql:8.0 service container, host 127.0.0.1 and a WP version matrix.

release.yml validates only that CHANGELOG.md contains the tag; PACKAGE_VERSION is still '1.2.0' at v1.2.1 and v1.2.2. The workflow_dispatch path derives VERSION from GITHUB_REF, which is refs/heads/main on a manual run.

scripts/install-wp-tests.sh is a hand copy lacking empty-password support; `[ ! -f wp-tests-config.php ]` at :130 tests the working directory. silver-assist-security wraps vendor/silverassist/wp-coding-standards/scripts/install-wp-tests.sh in 3 lines.

phpunit.xml hardcodes WP_TESTS_DIR=/tmp/wordpress-tests-lib while the install script uses $TMPDIR (/var/folders/... on macOS); WP_TESTS_PHPUNIT_POLYFILLS_PATH is relative; bootstrap hint says password 'root' and host localhost.

tasks.notes: WP 6.5 x PHP 8.2; WP latest x PHP 8.2/8.3/8.4; one WP_MULTISITE=1 job on latest.
coverage.xml ignored; phpunit --list-tests shows 24 tests and no duplicates across the unit, integration and all suites.

log.summary: Issue #48 opened and branch 48-settings-hub-hardening created and linked. Baseline verified against a real WordPress 7.1.3 test install: unit 16/16, integration 8/8, all 24/24 (86 assertions); also 24/24 with WP_MULTISITE=1. phpcs and phpstan pass; composer audit clean.

Phase 1 implemented. quality-checks.yml: removed `composer phpcbf || true`, mysql:8.0 service container on 127.0.0.1, new wordpress-version and multisite inputs, php -l integration-guide.php, unit and integration run as separate steps, coverage collected only on the coverage job. ci.yml: added WP 6.5 and multisite jobs. release.yml: PACKAGE_VERSION must equal the tag, manual runs use the tag input (checkout ref, VERSION, tag_name). Pins: checkout comments corrected to v7.0.1, github-script pinned to its v9 SHA. integration-guide.php: nested docblock turned into // comments (php -l passes). scripts/install-wp-tests.sh is now a wrapper over the shared script; phpunit.xml no longer hardcodes WP_TESTS_DIR or the relative polyfills path (bootstrap defines the absolute path); bootstrap hint updated.

Verified locally: unit 16/16 and integration 8/8 on WP 7.1.3 and on WP 6.5, 24/24 with WP_MULTISITE=1, run with no WP_TESTS_DIR set and from another working directory; phpcs and phpstan clean. The wrapper install into a clean TMPDIR created the suite and database on the first run. Not verifiable locally: the new workflow jobs themselves, which run on the PR.

PR #50 opened. All checks green on the first run: PHP 8.2, 8.3 and 8.4 on WP latest, WP 6.5, multisite, CodeQL and the security scan. Added the local quality script alignment and the coverage.xml ignore after the plan verification.

workItems.title: Phase 2: Test infrastructure and real integration tests
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-phase-2-integration-tests. Characterise current behaviour through real WordPress before any behaviour change. See the test list in the plan's 'Tests (Phase 2, extended in Phases 3 and 4)' section.
findings: Only 1 of 8 integration tests drives WordPress admin state (test_wordpress_admin_menu_integration), and it only asserts $submenu is non-empty.

Fake or vacuous: test_capabilities_check_for_settings_access (asserts core current_user_can only), test_admin_menu_hook_registration (admin_menu already has callbacks without the hub; comment about the constructor is false), test_plugin_callback_execution (calls the stored closure directly), test_tabs_navigation_with_multiple_plugins ($_GET['page'] is never read by src; active tab never asserted).

Unit tests also extend WP_UnitTestCase and need MySQL. Only test_enqueue_styles_on_silver_assist_page drives WP_Styles, and it asserts enqueued only (not src/ver); test_enqueue_styles_not_on_other_pages cannot fail because URL resolution returns '' without plugin_file.

Singleton reset is inconsistent (unit: tearDown, integration: setUp) and admin-menu globals ($menu, $submenu, $_wp_submenu_nopriv, ...) are never reset, so do_action('admin_menu') accumulates state across tests.
Coverage cannot be measured locally (no xdebug/pcov on the dev machine); CI has xdebug and uploads to Codecov with fail_ci_if_error: false and no threshold.

tasks.notes: Integration tests must read $menu, $submenu, wp_styles(), user_can_access_admin_page() or the callback WordPress registered. Tests that call render_dashboard() or get_plugins() directly go to tests/Unit: overwrite-same-slug, plugin_file first wins, the action-button cases and the escaping test.
Delete tests/Unit test_enqueue_styles_not_on_other_pages (passes with the filter removed). Extend test_enqueue_styles_on_silver_assist_page to assert src and ver. Phase 4 adds the exact-suffix test.
Informational only. The coverage gate is set in Phase 6 (task ci-coverage-gate), after the Phase 4 tests have landed.

workItems.title: Phase 3: Per-plugin capability
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-phase-3-capability. Implement then document. Design decisions (correct here if the owner disagrees): parent menu and Dashboard stay manage_options, filterable via silverassist_settings_hub_dashboard_capability; per-plugin filter silverassist_settings_hub_plugin_capability; invalid values fail closed to manage_options with _doing_it_wrong; validation regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ (no sanitize_key, it lowercases); cards and tabs filtered with current_user_can; Dashboard tab hidden without the dashboard capability; wp_die(403) guard in render_plugin_page; capability assigned after array_merge.
findings: src/SettingsHub.php:295, :307 and :322 hardcode manage_options; register_plugin() never reads $args['capability'].
IMPLEMENTATION.md:169, :250-280 and :1165 call the argument required since v1.1.1 and blame 403 errors on omitting it; that is false.
silver-assist-security/src/Admin/AdminPanel.php:262 passes 'capability' => 'manage_options' and requires the hub at ^1.2, so 1.3.0 is picked up without a constraint change.

WP core (7.1.3): add_submenu_page drops rows for users without the capability (plugin.php:1504-1507); user_can_access_admin_page checks the submenu's own capability (plugin.php:2234-2240); the top-level item stays and links to the first accessible submenu (menu.php:175-200, menu-header.php:157-173). Probe: editor reaches an edit_posts page under a manage_options parent, gets 403 on page=silver-assist.
options.php is gated by option_page_capability_{group} (options.php:29, :47); plugins lowering their capability and saving through the Settings API must filter it. Document it.
Existing unit render tests run as user 0 and will fail once cards are filtered per user; Phase 2 logs in an administrator first.

tasks.notes: Owns the IMPLEMENTATION.md "Error 2: 403" rewrite. Phase 5 only verifies it.

Must state: new capability arg and the two filters; get_plugins() entries and the plugin_actions $plugin payload always contain capability; render_dashboard() and the tabs show only plugins the user can access, so render_dashboard() with no logged-in user renders the empty state.

workItems.title: Phase 4: Code hardening
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-phase-4-hardening. Each fix lands with a test that is red before and green after; record the red run in the log.
findings: register_submenus() is not idempotent: firing admin_menu twice yields [silver-assist, early, early, late]. A plugin registered from admin_menu priority 10 gets no submenu in that request.

enqueue_styles() uses strpos($hook_suffix, 'silver-assist'), which also matches settings_page_silver-assist-security and toplevel_page_not-silver-assist-at-all; the first clause is redundant. Core derives the submenu prefix from sanitize_title() of the translated parent title.
__wakeup() is public and empty: unserialize(serialize($hub)) !== $hub.

Callback actions print raw output inside a <script> click listener with no event parameter, run at render time, can collide on button id (sanitize_key of slug-label), and the code comment says AJAX although nothing is wired.
PACKAGE_VERSION is '1.2.0' at v1.2.2 and is the stylesheet ver; v1.2.1 changed the CSS.
assets/css/settings-hub.css:299-303 queries the container element itself (@container on .silverassist-dashboard-grid), which can never match.

tasks.notes: PHPDoc of register_plugin() states the supported window. The long-form text is Phase 5 (IMPLEMENTATION.md, Registration timing).

Set PACKAGE_VERSION to 1.2.2 (newest released CHANGELOG heading). The test asserts equality with the first released ## [x.y.z] heading, skipping [Unreleased]. Phase 7 bumps to 1.3.0 together with the CHANGELOG move.

workItems.title: Phase 5: Documentation realignment
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-phase-5-docs. Apply the canonical-home table and the correction list in the plan. Leave historical CHANGELOG entries alone. Review with core-review --budget thorough until it reports nothing new. Additional owners from the plan verification: README absolute links (release zip lacks IMPLEMENTATION.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and integration-guide.php), README Development pointer, PHPUnit 9.6, action contract, tab_title/name/version semantics, multisite scope; IMPLEMENTATION.md Registration timing, plugin_file in examples, ^1.2, one update-button example; CONTRIBUTING layout, skip-db-create, composer test vs phpunit, spelling; .packagist.yml; SettingsHub.php docblock wording.
findings: IMPLEMENTATION.md requires PHP 8.3+ (:40, :95, :1147) while composer.json requires ^8.2; it embeds a stale changelog and version footer (:1322-1344) and claims built-in update support (:33).
'Settings > Silver Assist' in composer.json:3, the class docblock and copilot-instructions.md contradicts the top-level menu at position 80.

CONTRIBUTING.md and copilot-instructions.md describe a Brain Monkey fallback; README.md:19 and copilot-instructions.md:17,46 say PHPUnit 10 (the repo uses PHPUnit 9.6); the bootstrap hard-requires the WP test suite.
README Development section is duplicated (:450-512 and :514-554) with a stray fence at :512 and wrong test counts; the anchor IMPLEMENTATION.md#integration-with-wp-github-updater does not exist.
Install docs mix Packagist badges and plain composer require with the private vcs-repository requirement; CONTRIBUTING omits the token needed for dev dependencies.
copilot-instructions.md documents a non-existent `composer phpcs:fix`, a stale file tree, add_options_page and the Settings API, and Slevomat (a dev dependency no ruleset uses).

Undocumented: tab_title also labels the sidebar submenu; plugin_file is first-wins and fails silently outside ABSPATH; the Dashboard hook suffix toplevel_page_silver-assist; the action callback signature; the silverassist-settings-hub text domain is never loaded.
IMPLEMENTATION.md:351 describes onclick attributes; the code uses an addEventListener <script> block.

tasks.notes: Verify (do not rewrite) the Error 2 section that Phase 3 writes.
Class docblock "Settings > Silver Assist" and the PHPDoc at src/SettingsHub.php:179-180.

workItems.title: Phase 6: PHPStan tightening
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-phase-6-phpstan. Keep src/ fully clean; a tests/-only baseline is acceptable for the 2.x upgrade if logged as a follow-up.
findings: With reportUnmatchedIgnoredErrors: true, three ignore patterns are stale (Undefined type \WP_UnitTestCase, Use of unknown class \WP_UnitTestCase, Class .* extends unknown class WP_UnitTestCase).

With the ignoreErrors list removed: 106 errors (13 in src/SettingsHub.php, 33 in tests/Integration, 59 in tests/Unit, 1 in tests/bootstrap.php). src errors are array-shape casts (:141, :148, :384, :386, :398, :406, ...) and Constant ABSPATH not found (:267).
phpstan/phpstan is on 1.12.x (^1.10); szepeviktor/phpstan-wordpress already allows ^2.0.
The first ignore in phpstan.neon, `Right side of && is always true`, is still matched by src/SettingsHub.php:464 and must be deleted for the stated end state to hold.

tasks.notes: Record the Codecov percentage after Phase 4 has merged, then add a codecov.yml project status check at that value minus 2 points.

workItems.title: Phase 7: Release 1.3.0 and consumer verification
workItems.notes: Branch: 48-phase-7-release-1-3-0. Tags are immutable; never move or delete an existing tag. Order matters: the consumer verification runs before the tag.
findings: CHANGELOG.md lacks a [1.2.2] compare link and [Unreleased] still compares from v1.2.1.
The only consumer is silver-assist-security (requires ^1.2 via a vcs repository); its own SettingsHub integration test only checks that the hub resolves.

tasks.notes: Bump together with moving [Unreleased] to [1.3.0]; PACKAGE_VERSION is 1.2.2 until then.

Before tagging: in silver-assist-security require the merged commit as dev-main as 1.3.0 (or a path repository) and run its full suite (unit, integration, e2e if available). Tags are immutable, so this is the safety net.
After the release: composer update silverassist/wp-settings-hub in the consumer and confirm the lock resolves 1.3.0.

changelog.summary: Plan seeded from a four-track audit (integration tests against a real WP 7.1.3 install, capability design verified against core, documentation drift, CI and tooling). Lifecycle multi-session: the request asked for phases across sessions and the work lands as one PR per phase.
Phase 1 code complete locally; CI changes pending validation on the PR.

Plan corrected after an independent completeness and fact check: version plan made consistent (1.2.2 in Phase 4, 1.3.0 in Phase 7), coverage gate assigned to Phase 6, consumer verification moved before the tag, render-only tests moved to the unit tier, documentation owners and an out-of-scope list added, and several line citations fixed.
